newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador to adopt Convertibility Plan - Bucaram.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador to adopt Convertibility Plan - Bucaram.

text.p: Ecuador will adopt a Convertibility Plan pegging the sucre to the dollar in a four to one relationship and enforce strict fiscal discipline, President Abdala Bucaram said on Sunday.

"The big advantage of a Convertibility Plan is that it eliminates speculation on foreign exchange, reduces rapidly inflation and tends to equate interest rates in sucres with domestic rates in dollars," said Bucaram.
The Ecuadorean President said the Plan will begin July 1, 1997.
Bucaram said the sucre will lose three zeros and the new relationship will be four sucres to the dollar. Currently, one dollar is worth 3,519 sucres.
He said the new system will be based on strict fiscal discipline, higher taxes and less tax exemptions.
Argentina's former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, who implemented a Convertibility Plan in Argentina in 1991, served as advisor to Bucaram.
Bucaram also said he would seek to restructure $2.0 billion in debt with the Paris Club, increase the tax base and improve business legislation to attract foreign investment.
Bucaram added that he would restructure state oil firm Petroecuador, privatise state firms and seek a reform of the country's labor laws.
"This country needs structural reforms, to change not only state institutions, but also the mentality and behavior of Ecuadoreans," said Bucaram.
Bucaram predicted the Plan would help Ecuador grow four to five percent in 1997 and over six percent between 1998 and 2000.
He also predicted it would create some 600,000 new jobs between 1997 and 2000 and said that that would lift 1.5 million Ecuadoreans out of poverty by 2000.
Bucaram announced he would seek a constitutional reform to extend the presidential term from four to five years.
He also promised to scrap a 2.6 percent tax on loans and carry out 98 social projects at a cost of $135 million.
In his address to the nation, Bucaram asked for the cooperation "of all sectors" to help him carry out the new plan.
